text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- The French approach to unemployment would be disastrous for Finland, says Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto, suprised by the support Finnish socialists have shown for the French model.
- Industry's labour costs turned into decline last year, says study by Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).
- Bosnian refugess should not be returned against their will, U.N. human rights envoy Elisabeth Rehn says.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Broad EMU and soft euro would benefit Finnish export industries, sector representatives say.
- Problematic state of oil company Neste can be seen behind the discussion of merger with IVO, senior government official says anonymously.
- No synergy benefits to be found in merger between Neste and power company IVO, it would only prop up Neste, Finnish analysts say.
- Handling the central government's debt will be centralised to the state treasury.
- Efficiency of Finnish banking sector has improved to average European level, but further closure of branches may still be needed, central bank official says.
AAMULEHTI
- Centralisation of media ownership will countinue. The work of journalists should become sharper and opinions should be expressed more strongly, CEO of media group Aamulehti Matti Packalen says.
- Shareholders approved merger between Aamulehti and domestic commercial broadcaster MTV on Wednesday. New group due to start operations in 1998 will be called Alma Media Oy.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Negotiations to enlarge the European Union can start already by the end of this year, says Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.
- Hotline to report use of illegal material in the Internet to the police is planned, transport ministry official says.
DEMARI
- The management of the Finnish forestry industry holds the keys to a 1998 pay deal agreement, says senior official at Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
